newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares fall on foreign investment doubt.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares fall on foreign investment doubt.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.58 percent on Tuesday due to the continuing uncertainty surrounding foreign investment procedures.

"Some traders are afraid the Bank of Slovenia may limit foreign inflow but that is very unlikely. Therefore shares could start an upward trend as soon as next week," Karmen Korbun, a broker of bank Creditanstalt said.
She said the market was eagerly awaiting the government's decision on the procedure foreigners must undergo to buy shares in port Luka Koper, which was listed on Wednesday.
In the case of Luka, which is 51-percent state-owned, the government has to approve any foreign purchase.
"Until now the government has disabled foreign buying of Luka simply because it has not yet decided on the purchase procedure," Korbun said.
The 10-share SBI index fell 6.73 points to 1,152.7.
Nine shares fell, seven rose, one was unchanged and eight were untraded.
Turnover fell to 95 million tolars from 168.1 million.
Issue A of drug company Lek had the highest turnover, falling 2.23 percent to 18,450 tolars on volume of 3,065 shares for total turnover of 56.7 million tolars.
Financial conusultancy Primofin was the leadind decliner, closing 10.05 percent lower at 25,780 on volume of 100 shares for total turnover of 2.7 million tolars.
Ordinary shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the top gainers. They rose 4.17 percent to 12,000 on volume of five shares for total turnover of 0.06 million tolars.
Port Luka Koper fell 7.27 percent to 2,131 on volume of 4,202 shares for total turnover of 9.1 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana Newsroom, 386 61 1263 644
